transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump says he rejected Iran's offer to suspend conflict for seven days and reopen
the Strait of Hormuz.
He says the deal's not acceptable.
Iran wants the U.S. to lift its blockade and unfreeze billions of its money in foreign
banks in exchange for opening the Strait.
But President Trump says massive amounts of oil are flowing through the Strait now.
The oil flow is not consistent, and Piers Ayyabhatrawi says there are two things to
keep in mind.
"One is that Iran can and still does attack ships transiting through that narrow waterway.
So these ships are running dark with their transponders off to hide their location.
And that leads to the second point, which is that it's very expensive for ships to export
oil through the Strait of Hormuz because of those risks without a deal in place," and
Piers Ayyabhatrawi reporting.
Officials in the U.K. say they have arrested five men and foiled an apparent terror plot.
They're going over three vans discovered near an air base.
The U.S. uses that base to launch attacks on Iran.
The Senate is expected to vote today on a bill to reform college sports, and Piers Becky
Sullivan reports the bill would allow the NCAA to reinstate rules on eligibility and
transfers.
Supporters of the Protect College Sports Act say it's needed to rein in what they call
a Wild West era for college athletics.
Athlete pay has taken off since courts legalized name, image, and likeness payments.
Players can transfer freely between schools, and there are constant lawsuits from players
challenging eligibility rules.
The bill would grant the NCAA a limited antitrust exemption to restore those rules.
It also aims to prevent so-called superconferences by capping the membership of big revenue conferences
at 19 schools and disincentivizing schools from jumping from one power conference to
another.
House law experts tell NPR that if it becomes law, the bill would likely not end the flood
of litigation.
Instead, the bill itself is what would be challenged.
Becky Sullivan in PR News, Washington.
Forecasters are warning residents of Mexico's Baja Peninsula about Hurricane Polo.
The powerful hurricane could make landfall by late tonight.
From member station KJZZ, Nina Kravinsky has more from Hermosillo, Mexico.
Hurricane Polo has been making its way north off Mexico's west coast after rapidly intensifying
into a major hurricane.
The storm is expected to make landfall on the Baja Peninsula before making its way inland
to the Mexican state of Sonora across the Gulf of California.
The U.S. Embassy in Mexico warns travelers to be aware of flooding, mudslides, and road
closures early in the week.
The National Hurricane Center says moisture from the hurricane could also lead to heavy
rainfall and flooding in the southwest U.S.
After storm, Tropical Storm Rachel off of Mexico's southwest coast has been moving north
in Polo's wake and strengthened into a tropical storm Sunday.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Kravinsky in Hermosillo, Mexico.
You're listening to NPR News.
Forecasters say the nor'easter that pounded the east coast over the weekend is weakening.
One person was killed in New York State by a falling tree.
The powerful storm brought winds that were near hurricane strength, and it is still pouring
rain from New York to New England.
Last night in Los Angeles, singer Taylor Swift set a new record for the artist with the most
MTV Video Music Awards.
But the biggest winner of the night was an old-school MTV presence who headlined the awards
when they debuted in 1984.
And Piers Marie Andrusovic has more.
Piers Marie Andrusovic's new total is 33 awards, surpassing her own previous record of 30,
a tie with Beyonce.
She won the night's top prize, Video of the Year, and also became the first winner of
the Artist Director Award.
I've gotten to be a part of making 60 music videos, roughly 60.
Madonna scored the most wins for the night with seven, including Artist of the Year.
I spent the last year and a half finding myself, believing in myself, and really making the
music that I wanted to make.
It was 42 years ago that Madonna performed her hit "Like a Virgin" at the first ever
MTV Video Music Awards.
Marie Andrusovic, NPR News.
Fat Bear Week is coming to a close.
You have until tomorrow to vote online for the fattest brown bear at the Katmai National
Park and Preserve in Alaska.
The bears are eating to prepare for winter hibernation.
This is NPR.

topics.text: President Trump rejects Iran's offer to suspend conflict and reopen Strait of Hormuz
U.K. officials arrest five men and foil apparent terror plot near U.S. air base
Senate expected to vote today on bill to reform college sports and NCAA rules
Hurricane Polo strengthens to major hurricane, threatens Baja Peninsula and Mexico's Sonora state
Tropical Storm Rachel strengthens off Mexico's southwest coast following Hurricane Polo's path
Nor'easter weakens after pounding east coast; one killed by falling tree in New York
Taylor Swift sets record with 33 MTV Video Music Awards, surpassing previous record
Madonna wins seven awards at MTV Video Music Awards, including Artist of the Year
Fat Bear Week voting continues at Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska
